pages.transcription:
Feb. 1st 1941

Dear Mummy
I went to New York today and
saw Aunty and Uncle. It was very nice.
I hope you are well.
Love
and
kisses
Eva.

I certify that this is an
authentic autograf
of your daughter
Eva, very rare, as she
writes letters but very seldom
Stefan

Dear Hanna And Manfred,
Eva has just left after spending the day with us,
and she was as she has always been with us without any trace of shyness.
We told her that we were going to transfer her to another school and home,
and after making sure that it was not in Newyork itself - did she always
dislike the big towns like that? - she seemed to like the idea, although
she said she regretted a little having to leave that school and her school
friends. But I reassured her that if these were really good friends, they
could come and see her as New Rochelle and Croton are only about forty
minutes distance from each other. On the whole, I think, she likes the
change and I am confident that she will like it even better when she is
there. We told her that we have considered a change as that school there
was not the right thing for her and as she was rather lonely without
children in her age in the house. - But now you will want to know every-
thing about the new arrangement. I wrote you in my last letter about Mrs.
Schaeffer, the wife of the poet Albrecht Schaeffer (who lives in a little
summerhouse in the garden) who came here as refugees and have immigrated,
has taken in addition to her own children - three in school age and one
grown-up daughter who helps her - about a dozen or forteen other children
in various ages in her house and runs the whole as a large family, with
the help of two councillors and a married servant couple. I liked her very
much; that she is not Jewish and has six children, gives her a mixture
of detachment combined with motherly understanding and I have a
feeling that you would like her very much and that your ideas on the whole
are very much like hers. She said that except a few basic rules which she
strictly imposes - punctuality, writing home once a week, clean hands and
good table manners, no "funnies", no wireless except for special programs,
pictures only if there is something worth seeing and no chewing gum - the
children are free to do what they like. They have a few household duties,
make their own beds, help to serve at table, clean their own shoes, feed
the chicken, and that they are supposed to speak French one hour of the day,
the hour varying so that they get used to express themselves in different
circumstances, somehow brought me back our common life at Bath. At
first I was a little doubtful because there are no children exactly of
her age, but there are I believe two girls of ten and boys of 12 and 13,
and I think that will be alright.
pages.notes: Brief, Typoskript mit handschriftlichen Ergänzungen von Eva und Stefan Zweig.

pages.transcription:
2
Then I was for some time undecided about the school question, and I believe
I wrote you about it. But after making enquiries in various quarters and
being told that I should be glad if the "progressive" school would take her
as just this one has an excellent reputation, I decided for that one, the
more so as Mrs. Sch. from the beginning was more in favour of that one al-
though she said that the Croton public school was also very good and had a
very good reputation. - So we are going up there on Tuesday with Eva and
possibly Stefan, and if the interview with the headmistress is satisfactory,
I hope to have settled the matter so that you can be quite reassured. If
Mrs. Sch. tells me that they will probably keep her one or two days in the
school on trial to see whether she likes it, and should this not be the
case she can always go in the public school which, as I told you, is also
supposed to be very good. In that progressive school which is a private
school, we expect to get Eva a full scholarship. About the material side
Stefan has written to you. At Mrs. Sch.'s there is not very much to pay,
but it would of course be a relief for our relatives with their many
obligations if you would get permission to transfer a certain sum as a
contribution to your child's education. I was told that this can be done.
- Last week I went with all my doubts and problems to the Child's Study
Association (the address was given to me by Mrs. Haas) and I shall remain
in touch with them in any case, I had such an excellent impression of Mrs.
Cury with whom I discussed everything. She has lived in England, had a
school in Hamstead herself and has children who also, when they came over,
found the schools here so easy and so different. Somehow I have a feeling
that it is good to know someone in these committees who can advise and
might be useful in any little problems that may arise. - The Smollett
children I could not yet see, and please explain to Lotte that they live
about 20 miles out of Newyork, which takes some time if you have no car,
and as Mrs. Haas is busy with some charity work and wanted to make an
appointment days before, I could not arrange it this time as we had a lot
to do, I had many appointments about Eva and now we have not yet been to
Newhaven to look for a flat and will have to do it this week. - Please
inform also Mother that I shall probably not be able to write her a se-
parate letter this week. Next week we hope to be settled already and I
hope to find a flat which will also allow us to have Eva stay with us
for a little while when she has holidays again. Let me emphasise once
more that you should follow Stefan's advise that Manfred should take a
long rest in Bath after his exam in February. I think that he is quite
right that under no circumstances should you spend the beginning of spring
in London. We would feel so much happier if we know that you both are
taking a well-earned rest in Bath just in these next months after this
hard winter.

With best love and kisses

We have just been after months being ourselves
the healers and the others the listeners in Bruno Walters
concert in his box with a lot of ghosts from another life like
Mrs Stresemann and a singer which I heard first 42 years ago.
We had after that a nice talk with Walter and Erica Mann
your, Lotte
